Depth cues: fog, line width and eye-dome lighting

Source: R/depth-cue.R
depth_cue_3d.Rd

Configures the depth_cue argument of coord_3d(). Fog moves the colours of the plot layers toward a fog colour with their depth from the camera, in linear light, so far data recede. The same weight can thin strokes with depth, as scale_depth does in ggcube. Eye-dome lighting (Boucheny 2009) darkens rasterised pixels that lie behind their neighbours, which outlines silhouettes and depth steps from the depth buffer alone.

Usage

depth_cue_3d(
  fog = NULL,
  near = 0,
  far = 1,
  amount = 0.6,
  linewidth = FALSE,
  edl = FALSE,
  ao = FALSE,
  ao_radius = 0.25,
  ao_samples = 64L
)

Arguments

fog

Fog colour. NULL uses the fill of the theme element panel.background (white when it is blank); NA leaves colours unchanged.

near, far

Box depth fractions at which the fog weight starts to grow from 0 and reaches 1; near < far.

amount

Share of the fog colour at full weight, from 0 to 1.

linewidth

FALSE, TRUE (0.5), or a number from 0 to 1: the share by which strokes thin at full weight.

edl

FALSE, TRUE (1), or a nonnegative eye-dome lighting strength.

ao

FALSE, TRUE (1), or ambient occlusion strength from 0 to 1. Acts on shaded mesh faces with enabled lighting.

ao_radius

Positive ray distance in aspect-scaled panel units.

ao_samples

Positive whole number of deterministic hemisphere rays.

Value

A depth cue configuration for coord_3d().

Details

The fog weight of a primitive is $$w = \min(1, \max(0, (s - near) / (far - near))),$$ where \(s\) is the camera depth of the primitive's centre as a fraction of the depth extent of the panel box: 0 at the box corner nearest the camera, 1 at the farthest. Geometry fill and stroke colours move toward the fog colour by amount * w, and with linewidth a stroke's width is multiplied by 1 - linewidth * w. Panel furniture keeps its colours. The vector, raster and hybrid backends evaluate the weight once per primitive, so tessellated surfaces fade smoothly; view_3d() evaluates the same formula per pixel.

Ambient occlusion samples the hemisphere above each mesh vertex against a mesh bounding-volume hierarchy, following Pharr and Green (GPU Gems, chapter 17). Its accessibility estimates mean hemisphere transmission with deterministic rays within ao_radius, including face and texture opacity. Shaded face colours are multiplied in the shared kernel by 1 - ao * (1 - accessibility). The vector, raster and hybrid backends interpolate these values over faces. Both sides of a surface have their own accessibility. Text and label boxes keep their colours and draw last. The interactive viewer uses edl for occlusion shading.

Eye-dome lighting acts on the raster backend, the rasterised layers of the hybrid backend, and view_3d(). A pixel darkens by exp(-40 * edl * r), where r averages over its eight neighbours how far each lies in front of it in log2 of the depth normalised to the camera's near and far planes, as for geom_point_3d(render = "splat").

References

Pharr and Green (2004). Ambient Occlusion. GPU Gems, chapter 17. https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems/part-iii-materials/chapter-17-ambient-occlusion

Boucheny, C. (2009). Visualisation scientifique de grands volumes de donnees: pour une approche perceptive. PhD thesis, Universite Joseph Fourier, Grenoble.

Kitware. Eye-Dome Lighting: a non-photorealistic shading technique. https://www.kitware.com/eye-dome-lighting-a-non-photorealistic-shading-technique/

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = 1:6, y = 1:6, z = 1:6)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d(size = 2)
p + coord_3d(depth_cue = depth_cue_3d())
p + coord_3d(depth_cue = depth_cue_3d(fog = "grey90", amount = 0.8, linewidth = TRUE))
v <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 30), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 30))
v$z <- sin(3 * v$x) * cos(3 * v$y)
ggplot2::ggplot(v, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey80", colour = NA, shade = FALSE) +
  coord_3d(backend = backend_3d("raster", dpi = 72), light = NULL,
    depth_cue = depth_cue_3d(fog = NA, edl = 2))
a <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 7), y = seq(0, 1, length.out = 7))
a$z <- with(a, abs(x - 0.5) + abs(y - 0.5))
ggplot2::ggplot(a, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(fill = "grey70", colour = NA) +
  coord_3d(depth_cue = depth_cue_3d(fog = NA, ao = TRUE, ao_radius = 0.5))
